title: Aqua Teen Hunger Force Colon Movie Film for Theaters
full_review:
Clearly skewed to the 18- to 34-year-old male who likes his comedy surreal and peppered with raunchy non sequiturs, "Aqua Teen Hunger Force Colon Movie Film for Theaters" (First Look) is the feature-length version of the Cartoon Network's late-night cult hit, here untrammeled by not even the not-so-stringent standards of basic cable.

Writer-directors Matt Maiellaro and Dave Willis, who also provide some of the voices, revel in images and language that are meant to shock, albeit in a humorous way. Although it wears its sophomoric elements as a badge of honor, the inhabitants of "Aqua Teen," unlike those of "South Park," neither riff on pop culture nor offer ponderously shallow moral lessons. This is a self-contained world, based in a shabby New Jersey tract house, where the point usually is that there is no point.

With all that, there is still a coherent and conventional plot for Frylock (a floating, brainy box of fries), Master Shake (a milkshake who's mostly id) and Meatwad (a dimwitted and oddly flexible meatball) involving an exercise machine that spawns destructive alien robots, and an intentionally aimless subplot about their origins, lampooning the style of superhero epics.

Some of the gags are funny if repeated to death, and needless to say, there are the inevitable lifeless stretches that occur when a TV cartoon designed to be shown in 11-minute segments is stretched to 86 minutes. Even were it not for the flagged elements below, this highly uneven film would be strictly for die-hard fans.

The film contains a great deal of rough and crude language and profanity, pervasive sexual and scatological humor and an implied sexual encounter, cartoon violence and drug references. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
